During the pandemic, as remote work became the norm, Abnormal Security faced a common but critical challenge: staying connected with prospects and scaling their outbound sales in an entirely virtual world.

“Our reps were spending too much time connecting with leads manually, slowing us down,” recalls the company’s SDR Director, Joe Racine. At the time, the company implemented Orum’s AI Dialer to automate outbound calls, dramatically increasing their dials and meetings booked.
Initially, Nooks seemed promising—it offered a virtual office combined with a dialer for a lower price. However, the core function—speed and efficiency in dialing—quickly became a pain point.

Nooks’s reporting showed no delay when a prospect picks up, but when you listen to the recordings, it’s clear it’s there. The team was irritated by this; everyone already liked Orum’s dialer more and experienced a slightly faster connection. We liked Nooks’ virtual sales floor, but the heart and soul of what we do is to be able to dial and book meetings.

The lag time and inconsistent performance of Nook’s dialer impacted rep performance, leading to growing frustration across the team. Although Nooks had other features, they didn’t outweigh the fact that the dialer, the core of their sales process, was underperforming.

The decision to return to Orum wasn’t just about speed—it was about trust in the platform’s proprietary technology. Unlike competitors that rely on off-the-shelf, third-party infrastructure, Orum’s dialer is entirely proprietary, giving the company full control over performance and the ability to troubleshoot and innovate continuously.
